    Exactness of Hom into an injective module #

    A map into an injective module factors through f exactly when it vanishes on ker f. In particular, precomposition with f has image the kernel of restriction to ker f, so restriction identifies its cokernel with Hom(ker f, I) (LinearMap.cokernelEquivDualKer). This applies to presenting maps that are not monomorphisms, as occur in projective presentations over non-hereditary algebras. As a further consequence, an annihilator inclusion characterizes the existence of a linear map with one prescribed value.

    A map into an injective module factors through f exactly when it kills ker f.

    theorem LinearMap.range_lcomp_eq_ker_lcomp_ker_subtype {R : Type u} [Ring R] {P : Type v} {Q : Type w} {I : Type t} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q] [AddCommGroup I] [Module R I] [Small.{t, u} R] [Module.Injective R I] {k : Type s} [Semiring k] [Module k I] [SMulCommClass R k I] (f : P →ₗ[R] Q) :
    (lcomp k I f).range = (lcomp k I f.ker.subtype).ker

    Precomposition into an injective module has image exactly the maps vanishing on the kernel of the original map. The Hom spaces are linear over a semiring whose action commutes with the module action.

    noncomputable def LinearMap.cokernelEquivDualKer {R : Type u} [Ring R] {P : Type v} {Q : Type w} {I : Type t} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q] [AddCommGroup I] [Module R I] [Small.{t, u} R] [Module.Injective R I] {S : Type u_1} [Ring S] [Module S I] [SMulCommClass R S I] (f : P →ₗ[R] Q) :
    ((P →ₗ[R] I) ⧸ (lcomp S I f).range) ≃ₗ[S] ↥f.ker →ₗ[R] I

    Hom into an injective module turns kernels into cokernels. Restriction to ker f identifies the cokernel of precomposition with f with Hom_R(ker f, I). It is surjective since I is injective, and its kernel is the image of precomposition with f.
